topic: Feed lines and SWR (G9A; 11 pool questions)

questions.question: Which of the following factors determine the characteristic impedance of a parallel conductor feed line?

choices.A: The distance between the centers of the conductors and the radius of the conductors
choices.B: The distance between the centers of the conductors and the length of the line
choices.C: The radius of the conductors and the frequency of the signal
choices.D: The frequency of the signal and the length of the line

questions.answer: The distance between the centers of the conductors and the radius of the conductors

questions.question: What is the relationship between high standing wave ratio (SWR) and transmission line loss?

choices.A: There is no relationship between transmission line loss and SWR
choices.B: High SWR increases loss in a lossy transmission line
choices.C: High SWR makes it difficult to measure transmission line loss
choices.D: High SWR reduces the relative effect of transmission line loss

questions.answer: High SWR increases loss in a lossy transmission line

questions.question: What is the nominal characteristic impedance of “window line” transmission line?
What causes reflected power at an antenna’s feed point?

choices.A: Operating an antenna at its resonant frequency
choices.B: Using more transmitter power than the antenna can handle
choices.C: A difference between feed line impedance and antenna feed point impedance
choices.D: Feeding the antenna with unbalanced feed line

questions.answer: A difference between feed line impedance and antenna feed point impedance

questions.question: How does the attenuation of coaxial cable change with increasing frequency?

choices.D: Attenuation follows Marconi’s Law of Attenuation

questions.question: In what units is RF feed line loss usually expressed?
What must be done to prevent standing waves on a feed line connected to an antenna?

choices.A: The antenna feed point must be at DC ground potential
choices.B: The feed line must be an odd number of electrical quarter wavelengths long
choices.C: The feed line must be an even number of physical half wavelengths long
choices.D: The antenna feed point impedance must be matched to the characteristic impedance of the feed line

questions.answer: The antenna feed point impedance must be matched to the characteristic impedance of the feed line

questions.question: If the SWR on an antenna feed line is 5:1, and a matching network at the transmitter end of the feed line is adjusted to present a 1:1 SWR to the transmitter, what is the resulting SWR on the feed line?

choices.C: Between 1:1 and 5:1 depending on the characteristic impedance of the line
choices.D: Between 1:1 and 5:1 depending on the reflected power at the transmitter

questions.question: What standing wave ratio results from connecting a 50-ohm feed line to a 200-ohm resistive load?
What standing wave ratio results from connecting a 50-ohm feed line to a 10-ohm resistive load?
What is the effect of transmission line loss on SWR measured at the input to the line?

choices.A: Higher loss reduces SWR measured at the input to the line
choices.B: Higher loss increases SWR measured at the input to the line
choices.C: Higher loss increases the accuracy of SWR measured at the input to the line
choices.D: Transmission line loss does not affect the SWR measurement

questions.answer: Higher loss reduces SWR measured at the input to the line
